title: Prepare Data for ML and AI
objective: Prepare reproducible and secure training data by connecting its provenance, transformations, quality, and intended use.

sections.title: Preserving lineage from source to use
paragraphs: Before ingesting data sources such as S3, RDS, and streams, ML engineers verify the owner, update frequency, format, whether personal information is present, and intended use. A dataset name alone cannot explain which input, at which point in time, was used to create the training data.

When storing data, align the access pattern, capacity, retention period, encryption, and access permissions with the nature of the data. Recording the versions of the data and code used for ingestion, transformation, training, and evaluation makes it possible to trace model outputs later and rerun the process under the same conditions. Access-control metadata retained in RAG chunks is used to narrow the search candidates; during retrieval, the user's role and permissions are checked separately, and only authorized chunks are returned.

sections.title: Choosing Transformations and Preprocessing for the Intended Use
paragraphs: Classification, regression, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) require different input formats. For tabular data, check missing values, outliers, units, and category representations so that the same transformations can be applied during training and inference. Manage the rationale for and implementation of the transformations together with the dataset, without separating them.

When preparing documents for RAG, define the meaningful units needed for retrieval, update units, metadata, and access controls instead of vectorizing documents as-is. Chunking, embeddings, and vector stores affect not only search quality but also the ability to reference the original documents and prevent information leakage.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Data Transformation and Preprocessing

sections.title: Verifying Quality, Bias, and Integrity
paragraphs: Data quality checks examine not only the record count but also required columns, data types, value ranges, duplicates, missing values, label consistency, and how the data is split for training and evaluation. Instead of silently filling in data that failed inspection and proceeding, record the failure details, the affected scope, and the decision to correct or exclude the data.

Bias and class imbalance may not be visible from overall accuracy alone. Check the distributions and evaluation metrics for each user or data group, and investigate whether the cause lies in collection, labeling, splitting, weighting, or augmentation. Mixing evaluation data into training compromises the reliability of performance evaluation.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Data Quality and Bias

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for the demand forecasting model wants to explain which input data produced a given forecast result, even after the version of the ingestion source or transformation code has changed. What is the most appropriate approach?

choices.text: Save only the latest model and delete the training data and transformation history.
choices.explanation: This eliminates reproducibility and investigability of the output.

choices.text: Share only the dataset name and do not record the update time or provenance.
choices.explanation: It is impossible to determine which input data was used.

choices.text: Record and link the data source, data version, transformation code, training and evaluation data, and model artifact.
choices.explanation: Even after versions change, this allows the lineage from the inputs to the model and the scope of impact to be traced.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for an internal-policy search RAG application wants users to be able to trace search results back to the original documents. Which document-preparation approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Split documents into semantically coherent chunks and retain the original document identifier, update information, and access-control metadata used to narrow the search candidates in each chunk. During retrieval, separately verify the user’s role and permissions, and return only authorized chunks.
choices.explanation: This links search results to their source. In addition to narrowing candidates with metadata, the user’s permissions can be enforced through a separate authorization check before the results are returned.

choices.text: Combine all documents into one enormous string, remove provenance information, and embed it.
choices.explanation: The evidence supporting search results and the units for updates will be lost.

choices.text: Publish internal documents externally without checking access controls or applying any conditions.
choices.explanation: This does not meet data-protection requirements.

checkpoints.prompt: The evaluator of a recruitment-support model has confirmed that recall is low for a small group of applicants. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.text: If overall accuracy is high, do not examine results by group.
choices.explanation: This may overlook the impact on a specific group.

choices.text: Examine the data distribution by group, label quality, splitting method, and evaluation metrics, then improve data collection or preprocessing according to the cause.
choices.explanation: This allows you to investigate bias or imbalance hidden by the overall metrics.

choices.text: Add the evaluation data to the training data and see whether the metrics improve.
choices.explanation: This compromises the independence of the evaluation and overestimates performance.
